Ta có $\sin\left(x+\dfrac{\pi}{3}\right)=-\dfrac{1}{2} \Leftrightarrow \sin\left(x+\dfrac{\pi}{3}\right)=\sin\left(-\dfrac{\pi}{6}\right)$.\\
		$\Leftrightarrow \left[ \begin{array}{l} x+\dfrac{\pi}{3}=-\dfrac{\pi}{6}+k2\pi \\ x+\dfrac{\pi}{3}=\pi+\dfrac{\pi}{6}+k2\pi \end{array} \right., k\in\mathbb{Z}$.\\
		$\Leftrightarrow \left[ \begin{array}{l} x=-\dfrac{\pi}{2}+k2\pi \\ x=\dfrac{5\pi}{6}+k2\pi \end{array} \right., k\in\mathbb{Z}$.
